newsitem.title: USA: Clinton budget seeks $300 mln in new FAA user fees.
newsitem.headline: Clinton budget seeks $300 mln in new FAA user fees.

text.p: The White House's proposed fiscal 1998 budget seeks $300 million in new aviation user fees to recover costs to the Federal Aviation Administration that users do not pay under existing aviation excise taxes.

The budget plan said that is an interim measure until comprehensive financial reform, based on the work of the White House Commission on Aviation Safety and Security and the National Civil Aviation Review Commission, can be done over the next 18 months.
Starting in 1999, the budget assumed that the existing system of aviation excise taxes will be replaced by cost-based user fees to meet the FAA's needs.
"Such user fees are an important element of the Administration's effort to create a more business-like FAA," the budget plan said.
